\subsection{Manuscript 08: a trust-boundary summary}
The ordinary proofs establish the general theorems. The finite tests provide
evidence about the supplied implementations, including arithmetic signs,
indexing, tie resolution, and degree accounting. They cannot replace an
inductive proof of the compiler theorem. Conversely, the MRDP existence
proof does not certify that the software has generated a universal
polynomial: it has not. The delivered archive made this separation explicit in both
its README and its machine-readable report; the report README repeats it.

\subsection{\wtag\ Rerunning the suites in this report}
The programs are shipped byte-identical to the delivery but under prefixed
names (\code{code/07-quantum-mortality-*.py},
\code{code/08-probabilistic-laws-*.py},
\code{code/09-continuous-barriers-*.py}), and they import one another by
their delivered module names and write to delivered directories
(\code{examples/} and \code{verification/} for 07, \code{artifacts/} for
08, the named directory or \code{results/} for 09). They must therefore be
run on a copy with the delivered layout, never in place; the README gives
the commands. Manuscripts 07 and 09 need only the Python standard library;
08 needs SymPy (\code{data/08-probabilistic-laws-requirements.txt} pins
\code{sympy==1.14.0}). Rerun on copies on 30 September 2026 (07 and 09
with Python~3.14.4, 08 with Python~3.13.5 and SymPy~1.14.0), all three suites
passed with the recorded counts, and every rewritten output equals the
shipped file apart from line endings (the programs write CRLF on Windows)
and 07's recorded runtime. 08's report records the interpreter version it
runs under, so another interpreter changes that field too.

\section{Formalization}
\label{pqc:conv:formalization}
\wtag\ What ProveIt has formalized, and what it has not, is stated in
Section~\ref{pqc:conv:formal}. The three sources propose the following
plans; none of them has been carried out.

\subsection{Manuscript 08: proof obligations suitable for Lean or Rocq}
A direct formalization should keep the finite arithmetic layer separate
from the analytic probability layer. The following dependency chain avoids
requiring a large quantum semantics development before obtaining a useful
kernel-checked result.

\paragraph{Finite order and ratio layer.}
Formalize positive rational rows, least maximizing indices, and the
single-step equivalence
$h'q_i\ge hp_i\ (\forall i)\iff h'\ge h\max_i(p_i/q_i)$.
Induct on the horizon to prove the optimal product theorem. This portion
requires finite sums, ordered fields, and finite maxima, not MRDP.

\paragraph{Certificate layer.}
Define a finite index type for parameters and witnesses, an explicit
residual family of multivariate integer polynomials, and its sum of
squares. Prove that natural zeros force every residual to vanish. Prove the
selector lemma, the product invariant, and witness uniqueness. Derive the
cardinality formulas from the index constructors rather than from an
external count. Prove a compiler correctness theorem and use the Python
example only as an untrusted certificate generator.

\paragraph{Computability and MRDP layer.}
Encode the allocation interpreter and the threshold semidecision procedure
on naturals. The inspected \code{Diophantine.mrdp} interface can then
produce the finite polynomial existence theorem. A separate circuit
lowering theorem establishes degree at most four. This layer should not
claim witness uniqueness for a generic MRDP construction.

\paragraph{Measure and limit layer.}
Prove the prefix-cylinder allocation invariant and its measure identity;
then identify limits of cumulative masses with output laws. Prove the
variation bounds and the weak-computability realization with its explicit
nonuniform existential tail choice. Separate program extraction claims from
existence in classical mathematics.

\paragraph{Quantum layer.}
First verify the integer-linear gate recurrences and the quadratic norm
formula, with the state-vector dimension explicit. Then develop measured
first-return semantics using unnormalized branch states. The
operator-budget theorem can be formalized independently in a finite
Hermitian matrix library.

This is a plan, not delivered Lean source or a report of successful Lean
compilation. In particular, no guessed theorem names or placeholder
\code{sorry} proofs are included as though they were checked results.

\subsection{Manuscript 07: a realistic formalization decomposition}
A useful implementation plan separates five proof obligations.

\paragraph{Matrix block algebra.}
Formalize the block matrices in \eqref{pqc:qm:eq:packed}, the sum-of-Grams identity, and the projection homomorphism. These are finite algebraic identities. The normalization and word-transfer theorem can first be proved under an explicit hypothesis $B^{\mathsf T}B=Q$; no number theory is needed at that stage.

\paragraph{Rational factor existence.}
Provide a constructive $4d$ factor from a rational $LDL^{\mathsf T}$ decomposition and four-square certificates. A separate theorem can improve this to $d+3$ rows when the appropriate rational quadratic-form theorem is available. This isolates the classical dependency rather than concealing it inside a tactic call.

\paragraph{Exact word evaluator.}
Encode an integer matrix by finitely many signed natural coordinates. Matrix multiplication and lookup in a finite generator list are computable operations. Their graphs can be handled directly by polynomial equations or through primitive-recursive graph interfaces. One should explicitly state the chronological multiplication convention in the evaluator theorem.

\paragraph{Quartic certificate correctness.}
Prove that the residual family is zero exactly when the selected matrices and products are correct. Then prove uniqueness of the natural sign split and count the coordinate families. A sum-of-squares theorem produces the single polynomial. This is a direct finite proof and need not invoke the entire MRDP construction.

\paragraph{Unbounded bridge.}
Prove that the exact enumerator semidecides $\QMort_{4,7}$ and apply the public MRDP endpoint. An alternative route uses the existing \code{exactIter_dioph} and \code{existsExactIter_dioph} interfaces after representing the matrix-update relation \cite{proveit-trace}. These routes establish the same semantic property but need not preserve the same resource bounds or witness multiplicities.

No Lean source is supplied as ``verified'' in this package. A schematic statement with missing proofs would not add evidential value. The executable artifacts verify concrete instances and polynomial generation, while the general theorems are proved in the text.

\subsection{Manuscript 09: a concrete formalization plan for ProveIt}
\label{pqc:cb:sec:formalization}

The highest-value first formalization target is the finite checker and its
soundness, not a large universal machine table.  The mathematical architecture
has clean trust boundaries.

\subsubsection{Finite graph and polynomial layer}

Represent a finite vertex type, a source, a finite target set, and rational
weights.  Prove bottleneck/cut duality with finite paths and cycle deletion.
Then define \eqref{pqc:cb:eq:quartic} as an \code{MvPolynomial} over $\Z$.  Its zero-set
proof requires only finite sums, nonnegativity of squares, and the identity
$b(b-1)=0\Rightarrow b=0\lor b=1$ over integers.

An external graph search may propose a bit mask.  A proved finite checker
verifies source membership, target exclusion, and every below-threshold edge.
The proof assistant need not trust the search algorithm, its heuristics, or
its report of an optimal bottleneck.  When a claimed numerical lower radius is
used, the checker must also verify the stated rational crossing margin.

\subsubsection{Real rounding and geometric layer}

Formalize nearest-grid rounding in the sup norm and its compatibility with
closed rational boxes.  Keep the nongrid source as a separate vertex.  The
critical-radius infimum requires explicit nonemptiness and bounded-below
proofs; do not smuggle in the existence of an optimal real path.  The rounded
path argument then yields \cref{pqc:cb:thm:grid} independently of its length.

For the map compiler, certify a rational triangulation, agreeing affine
restrictions on shared faces, cube-valued vertex data, and row-sum bounds.
The critical global fact is continuity across faces.  A source file with
correct guarded formulas but an unspecified interpolation is not a proof of
the required map properties.

\subsubsection{Computability and MRDP layer}

Choose one canonical coding for rationals, finite tuples, finite tables, and
bit masks.  Prove the finite graph/cut predicate primitive recursive in those
codes.  A semidecider then enumerates mesh/certificate pairs.  At that point
the existing theorem \code{Diophantine.mrdp} is the correct public interface.
Its returned fixed polynomial certifies the encoded predicate, not a different
informal notion of safety.

No modification to the MRDP core is mathematically necessary.  Possible new modules in a
\code{RobustReachability} namespace would be \code{Grid},
\code{CutCertificate}, and \code{Diophantine}.  These names are proposals,
not existing or compiled repository declarations.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Source~18 proposes \code{PolynomialFlow} and
\code{KineticFlow} modules for its continuous-time certificates; the two plans
share the checker-to-MRDP layer (Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:formal}).

\subsubsection{Universal interpreter layer}

The final layer needs a concrete universal binary transition table, a verified
finite-tape semantics, and a proof that the chosen input coding matches the
interpreter.  One must separately establish exact simulation, terminal-slab
robustness, emergency timing, and the global map's Lipschitz bound.  The
universal trichotomy then follows from ordinary dovetailing.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}p{0.25\textwidth}XX@{}}
\toprule
Layer & Artifact that can be generated & Fact that must be proved\\
\midrule
Finite certificate & Vertex list, edge list, bit mask & The checked cut blocks all low-cost graph paths\\
Polynomial & Factored sum of squares & Its integer zeros are exactly admissible Boolean cuts\\
Geometry & Rational simplex table & Continuity, cube invariance, and a global error bound\\
Semidecider & Mesh/certificate enumeration & Acceptance iff the real critical radius is positive\\
Universal compiler & Interpreter table and its PWA image & Correct simulation and the three-outcome correspondence\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Generated data and proved semantics must remain separate.}
\end{table}

The present archive contained no Lean files, no claimed Lean build receipt, and
no axiom audit for these new results.  Its value for formalization is a small
set of explicit intermediate statements rather than a large untested proof
script.

\section{Further research questions}
\label{pqc:conv:questions}

The following questions are proposed research directions, not claims that
their full priority or open-status history has been settled by the present
literature search. They are ordered to put concrete extensions ahead of
broader conjectural targets.


\wtag\ The questions are printed by source: 08's twelve in
Section~\ref{pqc:conv:q08}, 07's ten in Section~\ref{pqc:conv:q07} (which
the source posed as subsections and are numbered here), and 09's ten, with
its recommended order, in Section~\ref{pqc:conv:q09}. How they overlap, and
which one another source partly answers, is recorded in
Section~\ref{pqc:conv:qoverlap}.

\subsection{Manuscript 08: probabilistic laws and normalization}
\label{pqc:conv:q08}\label{pqc:sec:questions}
\begin{question}[Kernel-checked unique quartic compiler]\label{pqc:q:kernel}
Can Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:singlefold}, including invalid-input rejection and the
exact count $5Nm+m+4N+3$, be formalized and connected to an executable
polynomial exporter in ProveIt? A decisive deliverable would be a checked
reflection theorem accepting the supplied $N=2,m=2$ residual certificate.
\end{question}
The finite positivity and tie-breaking lemmas make this the most sharply
specified implementation target. It need not wait for quantum semantics or
infinite probability theory.

\begin{question}[Smaller canonical arithmetic certificates]\label{pqc:q:smaller}
Can the $X,Y$ cross-product witnesses or the selectors be eliminated while
retaining degree at most four, natural-witness uniqueness, and a linear-size
arithmetic circuit? What trade-off between witness count, degree, and
coefficient size is optimal for this specific normalization predicate?
\end{question}
This is a finite compiler optimization problem. A mere MRDP existence
argument cannot answer its size or uniqueness requirements.

\begin{question}[Sharp multi-outcome variation budgets]
For a specified initial vector $p_0$, determine the sharp supremum of
$\sum_s\TV(p_{s-1},p_s)$ under
$\sum_s\Dinf(p_{s-1}\Vert p_s)\le B$. Does a useful potential formula
extend the balanced binary constant $1/2$ to $m\ge3$, and what paths are
asymptotically extremal?
\end{question}
Proposition~\ref{pqc:prop:variation} gives the universal upper bound $B$ but
Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:binary} shows that it can be substantially nonsharp when
the starting law is fixed.

\begin{question}[Uniform high-success realization]
What effective additional data are necessary and sufficient to turn the
existential high-success realization in
Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:weakclassification} into a uniform compiler? Natural input
formats include certified tail-variation bounds, an interior interval, or a
computable bound on the remaining logarithmic cost.
\end{question}
The present theorem explicitly leaves tail selection nonuniform. A solution
should specify its representation of real numbers and its promised inputs;
otherwise an apparent uniformization may hide an oracle.

\begin{question}[Exact symbolic infinite histories]\label{pqc:q:histories}
For which algorithmically described rational paths can $G_\infty$ be
computed, or bounded sharply enough to synthesize a desired success floor?
Examples include periodic transformations, linear recurrences, and
piecewise-rational paths with summable perturbations.
\end{question}
Finite prefix feasibility is decidable and uniquely certified here.
Certifying every prefix with one finite object is an additional mathematical
problem, not an automatic consequence of those certificates.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it, not answered: source~17's Theorem~\ref{pqc:rv:thm:rationality}
shows that a periodic binary environment gives a rational stationary root mass,
computed exactly as the fixed point of an affine map. That is a different
quantity from $G_\infty$.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-76 note (2 October 2026).} Bears on it; not
answered. For time-homogeneous finite-dimensional quantum loops, source~19
certifies every finite-path statistic of the infinite run by one finite object
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:iq:thm:moments} and~\ref{pqc:iq:thm:allmoments}), and its
Proposition~\ref{pqc:iq:prop:scheduled} shows that an arbitrary computable
schedule destroys any uniform Diophantine graph even in dimension one. Its
Question~\ref{pqc:iq:q:schedules} asks this question's ``periodic
transformations, linear recurrences'' for loops. $G_\infty$ is not treated.

\begin{question}[Operator certificates with controlled multiplicity]\label{pqc:q:operator}
Can an explicit quartic natural-witness system certify the optimal factors
$R_s$ for algebraic density matrices, including support changes, without
uncontrolled multiplicity from eigenvector choices? Can canonical principal
minor or characteristic-polynomial data replace arbitrary spectral bases?
\end{question}
The scalar earliest-maximum rule has no immediate analogue for degenerate
eigenspaces. Any proposed uniqueness theorem must address that issue rather
than merely add spectral witnesses.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-76 note (2 October 2026).} Bears on it, by analogy;
not answered. For a different operator, the group inverse $G$ and fixed-point
projection $P$ of $I-T$ for a quantum loop, source~19 replaces spectral bases by
fixed rank-free data: four quadratic identities with one solution
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:iq:thm:group}), adjugate coefficients on each rank stratum
(Proposition~\ref{pqc:iq:prop:rank}) and the Faddeev--LeVerrier
characteristic coefficients (Theorem~\ref{pqc:iq:thm:allmoments}), with a
unique-witness quartic. The optimal factors $R_s$ and their support changes are
not treated.

\begin{question}[Quantum front ends with structural compression]\label{pqc:q:frontend}
Which circuit classes admit polynomial-size exact Diophantine certificates
that avoid the full $2^n$ state vector? Candidate interfaces include
stabilizer structure, bounded tensor-network width, and a bounded number of
non-Clifford gates, with all compression assumptions stated explicitly.
\end{question}
The current state-vector checker is exponential. A useful result would
preserve exact zero tests and Born probabilities while making the source of
any speedup mathematically visible.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~10 (Part~VI) for bounded tensor-network width: for
a supplied contraction tree of merge-union width $w$,
Theorems~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:integer-tensor} and~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:cyclotensor} give
unique-witness quartic certificates with at most $(72m-64)D^w$ natural
witnesses and polynomial bit length per coordinate, hence polynomial size when
$w=O(\log m)$. Theorem~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:npconp} is the limit: a uniformly
polynomial-size compiler for zero output probability would give
$\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{coNP}$. Stabilizer structure and few non-Clifford gates
remain open (source~10's project~5).

\begin{question}[Interactive and compositional semantics]
How much of the projected-root representation survives for interactive
processes with adaptive inputs, correlated outputs, or sequential
conditioning? Can a compositional representation preserve joint laws rather
than only a terminal one-output marginal?
\end{question}
Independent samplers for marginals are not enough. A solution must preserve
the common probability space or the appropriate quantum instrument.

\begin{question}[Direct universal substrate polynomials]\label{pqc:q:direct}
Can one produce a fully expanded, audited quartic polynomial for a small
measured quantum controller or a stochastic fractional language, avoiding a
large generic interpreter? Which operation counts can be proved rather than
estimated from informal circuit descriptions?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:universal} gives a fixed polynomial in principle, not its
coefficients or a competitive universal witness count.

\begin{question}[Counting executions without counting arithmetic witnesses]\label{pqc:q:counting}
Can canonical finite source certificates be composed into useful
resource-bounded counting reductions while preserving projected-event
weights? Under what explicit restrictions can one obtain a genuinely
parsimonious unbounded representation?
\end{question}
The finite single-fold construction here is not a general unbounded
single-fold theorem. Any extension must confront that distinction directly.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~13 (Part~V) for finite horizons: its
compiler is parsimonious (natural zeros in bijection with accepted coin tapes,
Theorem~\ref{pqc:ql:thm:compiler}), and it proves a frontier: residual systems of
interaction degree two are counted in polynomial time
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:ql:thm:degree2}), while degree three is already
\#P-complete (Corollary~\ref{pqc:ql:cor:counting}). The unbounded parsimonious
question stays open.

\begin{question}[Continuous-time and robust physical semantics]\label{pqc:q:continuous}
Develop certified first-hit and deadline probabilities for effective jump
systems and computable flows, with explicit treatments of explosion,
Zeno behavior, exact equality observations, and robustness margins. Which
observables remain c.e. threshold events, and which cross the normalization
boundary proved here?
\end{question}
The finite-first-return interface identifies a tractable starting point;
it does not prescribe a physically preferred semantics for limit events.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~17 (Part~V) for exact stationary root
masses of discrete reversible chains: strict rational cuts are c.e.\ and
Diophantine, equality is co-c.e.\ and $\pione$-complete
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:rv:thm:cuts}), and arithmetic type is $\sigtwo$-complete
(rational, algebraic) or $\pitwo$-complete (irrational, transcendental;
Theorem~\ref{pqc:rv:thm:hierarchy}). Continuous time, explosion and robustness
margins remain open (source~17's Question~\ref{pqc:rv:q:physical}).
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~18 (Part~VIII) for
flows of rational polynomial ODEs: the finite first hit of an open rational
polyhedron is a c.e.\ event with complete canonical integer-tube certificates,
which also certify a positive tolerance to initial error and bounded forcing
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:equivalence} and~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:re}). Explosion is
handled twice: a certificate proves existence up to the event, even before a
blow-up (the pre-blow-up example of Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:examples}), and a
global mass-action lift moves every blow-up to infinite physical time without
losing a finite event (Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:globalchemical}). First-hit and
deadline probabilities, jump systems, Zeno behaviour and exact equality
observations remain open (Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:open};
Questions~\ref{pqc:tu:q:beyond} and~\ref{pqc:tu:q:boundary}).

\begin{question}[An algebra of probability specifications]\label{pqc:q:algebra}
Build a specification language that tracks whether a quantity is left-c.e.,
right-c.e., weakly computable, or computable, and automatically assigns a
sound arithmetic quantifier class to each comparison. Can successful
normalization-budget certificates improve the inferred class for useful
restricted program families?
\end{question}
Such a system would prevent the common mistake of compiling every
probabilistic specification to a single existential equation merely
because its source language is Turing-complete.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~13 (Part~V): quantifier normal forms with fixed
quartics for probability thresholds and finite mean
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:ql:thm:quantifiers}, equation~\eqref{pqc:ql:eq:meanquartic}),
and a transfer theorem that separates preservation of probabilities from
preservation of means (Theorem~\ref{pqc:ql:thm:transfer}). Source~17 supplies a
fully classified worked family, and source~10
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:cauchy} and~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:ast}) the
representation axis. No specification language is built.

\subsection{Manuscript 07: quantum mortality and its certificates}
\label{pqc:conv:q07}\label{pqc:qm:sec:future}
The following are proposed investigations, not assertions that every formulation is a previously catalogued open problem. Establishing priority and the exact state of the literature is itself part of the first stage of each project.
\begin{question}[Smaller rational instruments]\label{pqc:q:instruments}
Can the same unrestricted zero-word decision problem be shown hard in dimension three, or with fewer than seven outcomes in dimension four? A successful construction must avoid spurious zero products from any added normalization operators. It is not enough to simulate a computation only on a regular language of ``well-formed'' histories while leaving other outcome words unchecked. The projection-and-idle structure here gives a useful baseline for such an audit.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Residual-specific Gram compression]
For $Q(c)=c^2I-\sum_iM_i^{\mathsf T}M_i$, can one always choose rational $c$ so that $Q(c)$ has fewer than $d+3$ rational Gram rows? Proposition~\ref{pqc:qm:prop:sharp} does not answer this because it concerns arbitrary positive forms and does not respect the freedom to vary $c$. An arithmetic analysis of this one-parameter family could improve the quantum resource bound without changing the block argument.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Height bounds and practical rational factors]
The existence proof for a $d+3$ factor is effective by search, but the search can be enormous. Develop height bounds in terms of the bit length of $Q$, and compare algorithms based on rational isotropy, lattice reduction, and specialized four-square manipulations. The relevant output complexity is not just row count: the numerator and denominator heights of the Kraus operators affect both file size and the gap in \eqref{pqc:qm:eq:gap}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Choosing the lower blocks to preserve a shortest word]
Theorem~\ref{pqc:qm:thm:packing} confines the shortest length to a two-point interval. For a known source witness ending in $i$, equation~\eqref{pqc:qm:eq:erasuretest} says exactly when no extra letter is needed: $B_i$ must annihilate the preceding product. Can one choose a Gram factor with prescribed annihilation subspaces while retaining the same row budget? For unknown shortest witnesses this interacts with an undecidable search; for specified witnesses it is a concrete constrained quadratic-form problem.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Smaller explicit Diophantine certificates]\label{pqc:qm:q:smaller}
The formulas $71n+32$ and $72n+48$ are transparent upper bounds, not claimed optima. Eliminating known-zero matrix coordinates, exploiting the block structure, and using the final-active-letter criterion could reduce constants substantially. Such reductions should preserve the distinction between free matrix inputs and existential witnesses and should state whether the word-to-witness bijection survives.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[A complete proof-producing compiler]\label{pqc:qm:q:compiler}
Implement and certify the entire chain from a binary tag program and input word through integer matrix mortality, rational Gram packing, and polynomial generation. The first useful milestone is an independently checked rational Gram certificate plus a checked block-algebra theorem. A practical artifact should include exact source and target semantics, not merely display a polynomial with the desired informal interpretation.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The fixed-arity uniqueness frontier]\label{pqc:qm:q:frontier}
Can a useful restricted class of these instruments admit a fixed-arity Diophantine representation whose witnesses retain a controlled multiplicity? The bounded family already has unique arithmetic witnesses per outcome word. Unbounded trace compression can introduce arbitrarily many choices, and the general single-fold or finite-fold questions must not be claimed solved by the bounded construction. A sensible first target is a clearly specified instrument class with additional growth or normal-form constraints.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Promise problems robust under perturbation]\label{pqc:q:promise}
Study promises with a fixed separation from zero, bounded history length, or restricted coefficient heights. The estimate in Proposition~\ref{pqc:qm:prop:perturb} supplies an exact baseline for a finite-length promise, but not a length-independent robust undecidability result. A meaningful physical formulation must specify both the norm of the implementation error and what information about the exact reference model is available.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~16 (Part~VI) in the exact-synthesis setting:
positive-tolerance synthesis is computable with a computable length bound
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:net}), exact synthesis stays c.e.-complete inside
every open ball (Theorem~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:local}), and the length-dependent
threshold $1/(qD^n)$ is exactly where approximation becomes exact synthesis
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:gap}). Bearing on it: source~11 shows that
positive-tolerance transfer is always possible while no positive margin
separates its hard orbit (Section~\ref{pqc:rr:sec:bounds}), and source~10 that
exact zero is $\pione$-complete under Cauchy names
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:cauchy}). A length-independent robust undecidability
result for instruments is not given.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Decidable signed subclasses]\label{pqc:q:signed}
The nonnegative support argument gives one decidable boundary. Other restrictions worth investigating include simultaneous triangularization with arithmetic constraints, low-rank generated semigroups, or common invariant cones with an effectively checkable description. These proposals require care: positivity of operators in the Loewner order is not the same as entrywise nonnegativity, and either condition may fail to survive a change of basis.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it: source~11 (Part~VI) gives one signed (orthogonal) gate family
in which rational-matrix membership and the orbit of $e$ are polynomial-time
while the orbit of $\xi$ is c.e.-complete
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:rr:thm:main}); there the boundary is set by the source state,
not by a matrix class.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-78 note (2 October 2026).} Bears on it, not
answered: Part~I of the sibling report \code{stochastic-and-thermal-exactness}
treats strictly positive rational column-stochastic families, which share the
invariant cone of nonnegative vectors. For them it is undecidable whether some
finite product of at most eight such $7\times7$ matrices has rank one, even
under the promise that the generators have no common invariant complex line
(Theorem \code{ste:ee:thm:linefree}, Corollary \code{ste:ee:cor:seven}).
So the nonnegative-support boundary of Proposition~\ref{pqc:qm:prop:nonnegative},
which concerns the zero predicate, does not transfer to rank one: rank one in
dimension $n$ is mortality of the signed induced matrices in dimension $n-1$
(Proposition \code{ste:ee:prop:dimension}). A decidable signed subclass is not
given there.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Other exact scalar fields and tensor observables]\label{pqc:q:fields}
For a fixed algebraic number field with a chosen embedding into $\C$, exact field arithmetic can be represented by rational coordinate tensors. Determine how the Gram packing changes when conjugation and norms are expressed in those coordinates. The tensor identity \eqref{pqc:qm:eq:tensor} gives an elementary entry point for scalar matrix-product observables, but physically normalized tensor networks and general quantum channels with several Kraus operators per recorded outcome require separate semantic proofs.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~10 (Part~VI): exact arithmetic in
$\Q(\zeta_8)$ by four integer coordinates, with conjugation a signed coordinate
permutation and exact norms (Section~\ref{pqc:cc:sec:cyclotomic}), certified
tensor-network observables (Theorem~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:cyclotensor}), and a
single-valued sign gadget for $p+q\sqrt d$ (Theorem~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:sqrt2sign}
and the remark after it). How Gram packing changes is not addressed.
\end{question}



\subsection{Manuscript 09: continuous computation}
\label{pqc:conv:q09}\label{pqc:cb:sec:questions}
The following questions are concrete continuations of the results.  Some are
implementation or optimization problems; others may require new mathematical
ideas.  Their inclusion does not certify that no answer exists in the wider
literature.  A focused prior-art audit should precede any priority claim.

\begin{question}[Extract a fixed safety polynomial]\label{pqc:cb:q:extract}
Can the finite cut checker be compiled through ProveIt's existing machinery
into a fully displayed polynomial with an audited degree, variable count,
coefficient height, and witness-decoding procedure?
\end{question}
This is the most direct repository contribution.  Start with a deliberately
large but complete representation, then optimize.  The milestone is an
end-to-end proof that a zero decodes to a valid real safety statement.  A small
polynomial for just one grid does not meet the milestone.  No single-fold or
finite-fold conclusion should be assumed during optimization.

\begin{question}[Reduce the three-dimensional realizer]\label{pqc:cb:q:dimension}
Can one fixed continuous rational \PWA{} map of a square realize every
disjoint \cenum{} pair with the same exact-acceptance/positive-radius trichotomy?
What additional restrictions make such a realization impossible?
\end{question}
The current third coordinate provides an independently adjustable expanding
emergency channel.  Encoding that channel into the tape without allowing
spurious robust rejections is the central challenge.  Any lower-dimensional
claim must retain a positive margin on every rejecting input and must specify
a full continuous extension, not only a symbolic invariant subset.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Posed again, for strict contractions in dimension four, by source~14's
Question~\ref{pqc:sc:q:dimension} (dimension and observation minimality).

\begin{question}[Smooth and polynomial realizers]\label{pqc:cb:q:realizers}
Which regularity classes support the same simultaneous realization theorem
on a compact state space: $C^\infty$ maps, analytic maps, or rational polynomial
maps?
\end{question}
Smooth generalized-shift constructions suggest an accessible route for the
first class.  The polynomial and analytic cases cannot simply reuse the
constant terminal slabs: a real analytic map constant on a nonempty open set
of a connected domain is constant throughout.  One would need contracting
trapping regions instead of literal plateaus, with a new proof of the
positive rejection margin and a computably recognizable accepting target.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Partly answered by source~12 (Part~VII) in the scalar $2$-adic case: a
scalar $p$-adic contraction analytic near its fixed point has a uniform finite
extinction horizon (Theorem~\ref{pqc:ad:thm:analytic}, with explicit bounds for
rational polynomials in Corollary~\ref{pqc:ad:cor:poly}), so analyticity rules
out universality there, while flatness to all orders does not
(Proposition~\ref{pqc:ad:prop:flat}). Source~14's
Proposition~\ref{pqc:sc:prop:rigid} is the real homogeneous obstruction. The
real $C^\infty$, analytic and polynomial cases of this question remain open.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it only: source~18 (Part~VIII) certifies
finite open events of rational polynomial \emph{flows} and embeds them in global
mass-action kinetics, but constructs no realizer of the trichotomy, and a flow
is not a map of a compact state space.

\begin{question}[Extract and certify the rational neural circuit]\label{pqc:cb:q:neural}
Can the max--min representation in \cref{pqc:cb:cor:relu} be generated as a concrete
rational network, with a checked equivalence to the simplex table and useful
size bounds?
\end{question}
The elementary max/min-to-ReLU identities supply a baseline.  More important
than reducing depth initially is keeping a machine-readable correspondence
between the network, the PWA dynamics, and the certificate checker.  Noise at
hidden units should be treated as a separate theorem, not identified with
noise at the recurrent state register.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} \emph{Not answered.} Source~14 (Part~VII) gives an explicit integer ReLU
circuit, with $9m+2d_M-3$ gates, for its own contraction
(Proposition~\ref{pqc:sc:prop:gates}), not for the map~$F$ of
Corollary~\ref{pqc:cb:cor:relu}. Source~15 gives a unique-witness trace
quadratic that certifies the finite runs of any concrete rational clipped
network (Theorem~\ref{pqc:pm:thm:trace}), and $\sigma(u)=\ReLU(u)-\ReLU(u-1)$;
that is the certification layer such an extraction would need, but neither
source extracts this network.

\begin{question}[Quantitative transfers to genuinely different dynamics]\label{pqc:cb:q:transfer}
Can discrete symbolic, chemical, mechanical, optical, or hybrid simulators
admit effective noisy projection/lifting estimates analogous to
\eqref{pqc:cb:eq:transfer-radius}?
\end{question}
Exact Turing completeness alone is insufficient.  A useful positive result
would establish both directions of perturbation transfer, perhaps with a
controlled time rescaling, and specify which target is observed.  A useful
negative result would identify a substrate for which an exact simulator
necessarily destroys every positive rejection margin.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it: in source~12 (Part~VII) every finite quotient of the
$2$-adic contraction is nilpotent, so every positive-precision (clopen)
observation is decidable while exact extinction is c.e.-complete
(Proposition~\ref{pqc:ad:prop:nilpotent}, Corollary~\ref{pqc:ad:cor:complete}):
a data point for the negative direction, although source~12 does not formalize
this Part's noise radius on $\Z_2$.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it for chemical simulators: source~18
(Part~VIII) lifts every rational polynomial flow exactly to global rational
mass-action kinetics under a positive change of time
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:globalchemical} and~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:compressed}). That
is an exact orbit lift, explicitly not a noisy projection or lifting estimate
(Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:global}); source~18's
Question~\ref{pqc:tu:q:offmanifold} asks for such an estimate.

\begin{question}[Replace dense grids by small inductive regions]\label{pqc:cb:q:grids}
Can positive-radius inputs be certified by adaptive polyhedral partitions,
interval boxes, or algebraic invariants with substantially smaller witnesses
than the complete grid?
\end{question}
The current grid proves completeness but is deliberately expensive.  A
natural certified search starts with a coarse cut, refines only ambiguous
boundary cells, and carries a local Lipschitz bound for each relevant cell.
The theorem to preserve is completeness for every positive margin, not merely
success on benchmark examples.  The no-bound theorem excludes a computable
universal worst-case guarantee, but permits powerful subclass-specific bounds.

\begin{question}[Sharp radius--time tradeoffs]\label{pqc:cb:q:tradeoff}
Can the lower and upper exponential estimates in \eqref{pqc:cb:eq:time-radius} be
made comparable up to fixed constants or a fixed exponent for a universal
realizer?
\end{question}
The present lower bound uses a coarse global Lipschitz constant while the
upper bound uses the emergency multiplier three.  A construction whose
simulation and emergency expansion scales are matched could make the
smallest robustness radius a quantitatively sharper geometric encoding of
halting-time complexity.  Any such statement must specify the interpreter
and input-length convention.

\begin{question}[Classify exact critical-level reachability]\label{pqc:cb:q:critical}
For which subclasses is reachability at error exactly $\rho$ decidable or
characterizable, assuming $\rho$ is supplied exactly?
\end{question}
The contraction example shows that equality of the error budget to the
critical value need not yield a finite accepting path.  Compactness of the
state space does not bound the time variable.  Useful hypotheses might force
a bounded witness length or turn the relevant limiting chain into a finite
one.  A classification here would complement, rather than repeat, the
computability of the value itself.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it: source~12's Corollary~\ref{pqc:ad:cor:poly} gives a decidable
subclass, rational polynomial contractions of $\Z_p$, for exact reachability of
the fixed point.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Compare source~18's Question~\ref{pqc:tu:q:boundary},
the continuous-time question for equality targets; source~18's certificates
need open targets (Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:open}).

\begin{question}[Different noise semantics]\label{pqc:cb:q:noise}
What becomes of the Diophantine trichotomy for a single initial perturbation,
a fixed parameter perturbation, stochastic errors, total-error budgets, or
errors confined to specified coordinate directions?
\end{question}
Our fragile acceptance mechanism already uses only one perturbation in one
coordinate, but the rejection theorem controls all coordinates at every step.
This asymmetry provides a useful starting point.  Probabilistic eventual
acceptance, almost-sure avoidance, and existential noisy reachability must not
be conflated; their quantifier structures can differ substantially.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} Bears on it: source~18 (Part~VIII) uses a single
initial perturbation together with bounded measurable forcing, in continuous time
and up to a finite horizon, and shows that for open-target visits of rational
polynomial flows a positive tolerance of this kind exists exactly when the visit
happens (Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:equivalence}). It proves no trichotomy and
treats no stochastic or total-error budget.

\begin{question}[Geometry of the fragile boundary]\label{pqc:cb:q:boundary}
What can be said about the topology, dimension, or effective descriptive
complexity of the full set $\{x:\neg\Hit(x),\rho_F(x,H)=0\}$, beyond the
$\Pi^0_1$-complete classification on the encoded inputs?
\end{question}
On regions disjoint from $H$, the critical radius is Lipschitz by
\cref{pqc:cb:prop:value-stability}, so its positive set is open.  The coded-input
classification does not by itself determine the measure or fractal geometry
of the full zero set.  Studying that geometry could connect certificate
complexity with dynamical notions of chain accessibility.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-62 note (30 September 2026).} Posed again, for different zero sets, by source~12's
Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:measure} and source~14's
Question~\ref{pqc:sc:q:zeroset}.

\paragraph{Recommended order.}
First formalize the finite graph and quartic checker, then the rounding
soundness theorem, and only then extract a fixed MRDP polynomial.  In parallel,
make one concrete interpreter table and the neural representation explicit.
Dimension reduction and polynomial realizations are better treated as
separate mathematical projects after these certified baselines exist.

\subsection{\wtag\ How the questions overlap}
\label{pqc:conv:qoverlap}
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Partly answered.} Question~\ref{pqc:q:continuous} (08) asks
which observables of computable flows and jump systems remain c.e.
threshold events once robustness margins are treated explicitly. For
discrete-time rational piecewise-affine maps under adversarial per-step
noise, Part~III answers the robustness part: positive margin is
$\sigone$-complete with complete quartic certificates, and noise-fragile
nonacceptance is $\pione$-complete, hence not existential Diophantine
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:cb:thm:quartic} and~\ref{pqc:cb:thm:classification},
Corollary~\ref{pqc:cb:cor:dioph-trichotomy}). The question stays open for
continuous time, jump processes, deadlines, explosion and stochastic noise,
which is also 09's Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:noise}.
\wtag\ \emph{Batch-64 note (30 September 2026).} For continuous time it is now
partly answered by Part~VIII: finite open first-hit events of rational
polynomial flows are c.e.\ with complete, positively robust integer
certificates, and explosion is handled; probabilities, deadlines, Zeno and
equality events remain open (the note after Question~\ref{pqc:q:continuous}).
\item \emph{One frontier, two forms.} 08's
Question~\ref{pqc:q:counting} and 07's Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:frontier}
both ask for a fixed-arity representation with controlled witness
multiplicity; 09 (Section~\ref{pqc:cb:sec:cuts}) likewise declines to
claim it. The sibling report
\code{canonical-diophantine-certificates} of this category shows that a
single-fold (finite-fold) universal halting polynomial exists exactly when
every \cenum{} set has such a representation, an open problem.
\item \emph{Extraction of a fixed polynomial.} 08's
Question~\ref{pqc:q:direct}, 07's Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:compiler} and 09's
Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:extract} ask for explicit, audited forms of the three
different fixed polynomials of Remark~\ref{pqc:conv:rem:fixedpoly}.
\item \emph{Smaller explicit certificates.} 08's
Question~\ref{pqc:q:smaller} and 07's Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:smaller} ask
the same kind of question for the two different explicit quartic families
$F_{N,m}$ and $\mathscr Q_{D,K,n}$.
\item \emph{Formalization first.} 08's Question~\ref{pqc:q:kernel}, 07's
milestone in Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:compiler} and 09's recommended order
all put a kernel-checked finite certificate layer before any unbounded
statement.
\item \wtag\ \emph{Partly answered in Parts V--VII} (batch~62; the notes after
each question give the details): Question~\ref{pqc:q:frontend} by source~10
(bounded tensor width) with the $\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{coNP}$ limit;
Question~\ref{pqc:q:fields} by source~10 ($\Q(\zeta_8)$ coordinates and
$\Q(\sqrt d)$ signs); Question~\ref{pqc:q:promise} by source~16 (exact synthesis
versus approximation); Question~\ref{pqc:q:counting} and
Question~\ref{pqc:q:algebra} by source~13; Question~\ref{pqc:q:continuous} by
source~17 (stationary masses); Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:realizers} by source~12
(scalar $2$-adic analytic contractions). Questions~\ref{pqc:q:histories},
\ref{pqc:q:signed}, \ref{pqc:cb:q:dimension}, \ref{pqc:cb:q:transfer},
\ref{pqc:cb:q:critical} and~\ref{pqc:cb:q:boundary} are only borne on, and
Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:neural} is \emph{not} answered: sources~14 and~15 supply
a gate count for another map and a certification layer, not the network.
Questions~\ref{pqc:q:smaller}, \ref{pqc:q:instruments}, the variation-budget
and high-success questions are not addressed.
\item \wtag\ \emph{Batch 64: Part VIII} (dated notes of 30 September 2026 after
each question): Question~\ref{pqc:q:continuous} is partly answered by
source~18 (open first-hit events of rational polynomial flows);
Questions~\ref{pqc:cb:q:realizers}, \ref{pqc:cb:q:transfer},
\ref{pqc:cb:q:critical} and~\ref{pqc:cb:q:noise} are only borne on. Source~18's
own questions (Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:questions}) carry pointers to
Questions~\ref{pqc:q:kernel}, \ref{pqc:q:direct}, \ref{pqc:q:smaller},
\ref{pqc:qm:q:smaller}, \ref{pqc:cb:q:grids} and~\ref{pqc:cb:q:tradeoff}.
\item \wtag\ \emph{Infinite paths and liveness} (batch-64 note, 30 September
2026). This report's infinite-time statements are almost-sure termination and
probabilistic thresholds (Part~I, $\pitwo$ in
Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:unconditionaltable}), robust avoidance and noise-fragile
divergence (Part~III), and stationary masses (Part~V). The third report of this
category, \code{liveness-beyond-halting} (written in \code{2a34b1740}),
classifies infinite-path properties of computable finitely branching systems: a
fixed computable progress deadline is $\pione$, bounded gaps $\sigtwo$, some
computable deadline $\Sigma^0_3$, recurrence (B\"uchi acceptance)
$\Sigma^1_1$-complete and deterministic recurrence $\pitwo$ (its Theorems
\code{lbh:thm:hierarchy} and \code{lbh:thm:deterministic}); a shared computable
deadline makes recurrence an effectively closed condition (\code{lbh:thm:compact}),

\section{Conclusions}
\label{pqc:conv:conclusion}

\subsection{Manuscript 08}
The useful extension of Diophantine computation is not just another
unconventional universal instruction set. It is a semantics-preserving
account of which quantitative assertions admit finite arithmetic witnesses.
Effective output laws admit a common projected-root representation, but
normalization can raise a strict threshold from $\sigone$ to
$\sigtwo$, even with a success guarantee arbitrarily close to one.

The exact normalization budget supplies a constructive organizing theorem:
accumulated mass can follow a prescribed positive conditional path exactly
when its product of maximal coordinate ratios fits the available budget.
That theorem yields a direct, unique-witness quartic compiler, a sharp
binary oscillation bound, an exact weak-computability characterization,
and a noncommutative operator-order extension. The explicit finite compiler
and tests are ready to serve as a concrete formalization target; the broader
universal and quantum results retain their stated existence and semantic
boundaries.

\subsection{Manuscript 07}
The key quantitative step is to distribute rational Gram rows among the original active Kraus operators instead of allocating a large correction block to each one. Exact normalization then costs only $\lceil s/k\rceil$ additional state-space coordinates for an $s$-row factor. Classical rational quadratic-form theory supplies $s=d+3$, while an elementary implementation supplies $s=4d$.

This produces a proof of quantum zero-word undecidability in dimension four with seven rational outcomes, based on the published six-generator matrix theorem. Its witness transformation is unusually tight: erase idle outcomes in one direction, and append one active outcome in the other. The polynomial compiler subsequently records exact signed products, not merely legal paths, with quartic degree and explicit linear-in-length witness counts.

The work therefore extends the repository's Diophantine program toward an interference-based computational substrate without conflating exact mathematics, finite experimental precision, and formal proof status. The row-packing theorem is ready for independent mathematical review; the elementary branch and the bounded quartic compiler are ready for focused formalization.

\subsection{Manuscript 09}
The main contribution is not another bare invocation of MRDP on a halting
set.  It is a finite certificate architecture for a genuinely infinite-time
property, together with a universal dynamical construction that proves the
architecture's exact expressive boundary.

Positive critical radius is witnessed by a finite graph cut and hence by an
explicit quartic equation at some mesh.  A fixed MRDP polynomial exists for
the resulting enumerable predicate.  One fixed three-dimensional continuous
rational map realizes arbitrary disjoint enumerable acceptance and robust
rejection sets, while the remaining inputs diverge without any positive
noise margin.  Its radius is numerically computable with an error bound that
does not depend on trajectory length, yet deciding whether the value is
positive is maximally hard among enumerable problems.  An exact rational
neural update block inherits the same statement under the specified output
noise semantics.

The result is therefore both constructive and limiting: finite arithmetic
witnesses can certify robust nonacceptance of a continuous universal computer,
but they cannot provide a complete existential certification of its fragile
divergence.  The distinction survives even when the numerical value separating
the outcomes is a computable Lipschitz function.

\part{Exact probabilities: well-conditioned quartic landscapes and reversible equilibria (sources 13 and 17)}
\label{pqc:part:b62-V}

\section{\wtag\ Conventions of Part V}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-V}

Part~V prints two manuscripts of batch~62 in full: source~13, \emph{Probabilities
from Well-Conditioned Quartics} (batch-62 manuscript~09), and source~17,
\emph{Arithmetic of Rapidly Mixing Reversible Computation} (batch-62
manuscript~14). Both concern exact probabilities of effective stochastic
systems, the subject of Part~I. Source~13 turns the probability that a
fair-coin computation halts by time $t$ into $2^{-t}$ times the root count,
component count or Euler characteristic of an explicit, uniformly
well-conditioned quartic. Source~17 builds reversible birth--death chains with
a sharp common spectral gap whose exact stationary root mass nevertheless
carries halting, eventual periodicity and a rational/Liouville dichotomy.
Source numbers are this report's own: the shipped files of source~NN carry the
prefix \code{NN-}, and the batch-62 manuscript numbers are recorded in
Appendix~\ref{pqc:app:provenance}. Source~13 was written from the pin
\code{b998f70c6} and source~17 from \code{e18718e83}, the commit that wrote
Parts~I--IV; source~17 cites those Parts, source~13 does not.

\subsection{What is printed once, and where Part I is re-derived}
Neither source contradicts Part~I. Where they re-derive it, Part~I's statement
is cited and the source's argument is kept as a second route:
\begin{itemize}
\item Source~13's quantifier table re-derives
Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:unconditionaltable} (the interior thresholds
$0<q<1$), with the same totality sampler~\eqref{pqc:eq:te}. That table is not
reprinted; only its rows for $p=1$, $p=0$ and finite mean, which Part~I does
not print, are kept (Section~\ref{pqc:ql:sec:normalforms}). Its quartic
normalization is Lemma~\ref{pqc:lem:quarticlower}, its fixed lower-cut quartic
is Corollary~\ref{pqc:cor:strict} for this model, and the characterization half
of its realization theorem is Theorem~\ref{pqc:thm:semimeasure}; the uniform
geometric constants of that theorem are new.
\item Source~17's Theorems~\ref{pqc:rv:thm:halting} and~\ref{pqc:rv:thm:cuts}
(strict cuts $\sigone$-complete, equality $\pione$-complete) are
Proposition~\ref{pqc:prop:totalcuts} transplanted to exact stationary masses,
with the same halting-time device. The setting (reversibility, a sharp common
spectral gap, rational-valued hard instances) is new.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Three finite-horizon probability representations.}
Three different ways of reading a finite-horizon probability off a polynomial
occur in this category, and they must not be mixed. Part~I writes an output law
as the dyadic mass of the projection of \emph{one fixed} quartic,
$\mu_e(z)=\sum_c2^{-\ell(c)}[\exists w\;U(e,z,c,w)=0]$
(equation~\eqref{pqc:eq:rootmass}); witnesses need not be unique and are never
counted. Source~13 uses a horizon-dependent quartic $\cE_{e,x,t}$ whose natural
zeros are in bijection with the accepted $t$-bit coin tapes, so that
$p_{e,x,t}=2^{-t}\#\{\text{zeros}\}$
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:ql:thm:stochastic}); runs that halt early are padded with
\emph{random} bits. The sibling report \code{canonical-diophantine-certificates}
(its Theorem with label \code{cdc:mem:thm:probability}) counts canonically
stopped roots with weights $2^{T-\tau}$. The tempting false reading is to divide
a \emph{canonically padded} root count by $2^T$: that report shows this is wrong,
because a canonically stopped run has one root however early it halts. Source~13
pads with random bits, so every early-halting run contributes its $2^{t-h}$
extensions and its unweighted count divided by $2^t$ is right
(Section~\ref{pqc:ql:sec:stochastic}).
