\subsection{Source 17: rapidly mixing reversible computation}
\label{pqc:rv:sec:questions}
The following questions are proposed continuations of this construction.
They are not all asserted to be previously published open problems.
They specify what would constitute a further theorem or a useful
implementation, rather than treating a finite experiment as a result.

\begin{question}[A small kernel-checked equilibrium certificate]
Can the compact prefix checker, its unique-witness theorem and its
real-interval semantics be formalized together as a short independent
module? The first target is \cref{pqc:rv:thm:compact} linked to
\cref{pqc:rv:thm:prefix}, not a full Markov-chain library. A useful deliverable
would accept a concrete prefix certificate and return a theorem
about the exact infinite equilibrium.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:kernel}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[A reusable sharp half-line gap theorem]
How generally can \cref{pqc:rv:lem:poincare} be formalized and extended?
For varying death probabilities bounded below by $q$, the same
convolution estimate still suggests a direct lower bound. A sharper
result could use nonuniform products of ratios rather than a single
worst-case $r$, with mechanically checkable drift certificates.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Compiling sparse arithmetic type into fixed local rules]
The one-defect computation has an explicit finite guarded-affine
realization. Can the rational--Liouville dichotomy be realized by one
fixed universal local rule set, with a proved clock schedule preserving
superlacunarity in the actual microstep index? Simply computing a
factorial target in an auxiliary counter does not automatically give
the required gap between defect times after compilation.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Algebraic irrational points in the equilibrium Cantor set]
Does $\mathcal C$ contain an algebraic irrational number? Equivalently,
does $\mathcal K$ contain one, or can an algebraic irrational in
$[0,2/3]$ have a binary expansion containing no consecutive ones?
The sparse and low-complexity results exclude large explicit classes
but do not answer this full question. The relation to digit restrictions
and the algebraic-number complexity theorem \cite{b62s17-ab} is direct;
no conclusion for arbitrary high-complexity expansions is claimed.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Irrationality exponents of explicit equilibria]
Determine the irrationality exponent of the Thue--Morse equilibrium
in \cref{pqc:rv:eq:tm}, or prove finite upper and lower bounds beyond
irrationality. Transcendence from digit complexity does not itself
supply the desired approximation exponent after the variable-length
coding and reciprocal transformation.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Decidable restricted environment languages]
For specific finite descriptions, such as automatic sequences,
substitutions or bounded-state transducers, determine the complexity
of eventual periodicity and therefore of exact rationality of the
root mass. The unrestricted $\Sigma^0_2$ result does not prevent
strong algorithms on restricted descriptions. Any claimed algorithm
must specify the environment language and its promise conditions.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Coefficient size versus witness count]
The full presentation uses $3N+4$ witnesses and small recurrence
coefficients; the compact presentation uses $N+1$ witnesses and
coefficients with $O(N)$ bits. Can one improve this tradeoff while
retaining total degree four, a unique natural witness and a transparent
prefix semantics? Lower bounds would require a clearly fixed encoding
model, since substitutions and auxiliary coordinates can shift costs.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:smaller}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Beyond root mass]
What are the exact arithmetic complexities of stationary entropy,
resolvent entries, moments and asymptotic variance in the same family?
Many such quantities have effective tail bounds, but their equality
and arithmetic-type predicates need separate reductions. One should
not infer their complexity merely from the root-mass construction.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Sampling and rare defects]
Quantify the sample or trajectory length needed to distinguish a
zero-defect chain from a defect at time $T$ with a prescribed error
probability. The stationary root-mass separation is exactly
\cref{pqc:rv:eq:separation}; a path can additionally reveal a defect by
visiting it. Comparing these two observation models could clarify
which statistical costs coexist with the common mixing rate.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Physical and continuous-time realizations]\label{pqc:rv:q:physical}
Which analogues persist for continuous-time birth--death chains with
uniformly bounded rational rates, or for explicitly constrained
reaction and queueing models? Uniformizing a specified continuous-time
kernel is straightforward, but implementing the programmable environment
using a physically restricted finite reaction language is a different
problem. The cost of a zero test and of history arithmetic must be
accounted for rather than concealed in a rate function.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:continuous}, which this source partly answers for discrete reversible chains.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Fixed-arity multiplicity control]
Can any nontrivial restricted class of these strict equilibrium cuts
be compiled to fixed-arity polynomials with finite-fold or single-fold
witness control? The fixed-horizon uniqueness result is insufficient:
there can be arbitrarily many certifying horizons and evaluator
encodings. A useful advance would either identify a restricted class
with a complete construction or prove a precise obstruction.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:counting} and the fixed-arity compression question of the sibling report \code{canonical-diophantine-certificates}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Robust arithmetic predicates]
Which meaningful equilibrium properties admit decision procedures
under an explicit separation promise? For example, a known positive
gap from a rational threshold makes a strict comparison decidable by
\cref{pqc:rv:thm:prefix}. Rationality and algebraicity are not open properties;
formulating useful robust replacements, with certificate sizes and
input representations specified, may be more fruitful than seeking
an impossible exact decision procedure.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:algebra}.
\end{question}


\part{Exact gates: cyclotomic contraction certificates, exact synthesis and state transfer (sources 10, 11 and 16)}
\label{pqc:part:b62-VI}

\section{\wtag\ Conventions of Part VI}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-VI}

Part~VI prints three manuscripts of batch~62. Source~10, \emph{Diophantine
Certificates for Coherent Computation} (batch-62 manuscript~06), certifies whole
coherent tensor contractions over $\Z[e^{i\pi/4}]$ with unique natural
witnesses, and so supplies the witness counts that Part~II's quantum front end
leaves open. Sources~11, \emph{Decidable Gates, Undecidable State Transfer}
(batch-62 manuscript~07), and~16, \emph{Dense Rotations, Undecidable Exactness}
(batch-62 manuscript~13), study exact computation with a fixed finite set of
rational four-dimensional rotations. They were written independently, from the
pins \code{b6bf6406a} and \code{e18718e83}, and neither cites the other or
Parts~I--IV; source~10 was written from \code{ccfb084ad}.

\subsection{How sources 11 and 16 are merged}
\label{pqc:gates:sec:plan}
Sources~11 and~16 share one arithmetic core. Both evaluate the free group on
two letters at the same quaternions $(3+4i)/5$ and $(3+4j)/5$, prove the same
modulo-five denominator rigidity theorem, decode words by the same residue
calculation, embed free groups of every finite rank by conjugates $a^jba^{-j}$,
and turn a finite group presentation into rotation gates by the same Mihailova
fiber-product compiler. That core is printed once, in
Section~\ref{pqc:gates:sec:core}. Where the two sources state the same result,
one statement carries both sources' labels, one proof is printed, and a
genuinely different proof is kept as a marked second route. Where they differ in
normalization (source~11 indexes generators from $0$, source~16 from $1$) or in
the statement proved, both are printed.

The two sources then specialize the compiler in opposite directions, and both
specializations are printed in full:
\begin{itemize}
\item Source~11 (Sections~\ref{pqc:rr:sec:orbit}--\ref{pqc:rr:sec:bounds})
compiles a Miller group, whose word problem is decidable in polynomial time and
whose marked conjugacy is c.e.-complete: rational-matrix membership in the gate
group is polynomial-time, while exact transfer from one fixed rational state is
c.e.-complete, and the hard targets satisfy an order-five recurrence.
\item Source~16 (Sections~\ref{pqc:dr:sec:universal}--\ref{pqc:dr:sec:dimension})
compiles a group $G_0*\langle t\rangle$ with c.e.-complete word problem:
rational-matrix membership itself is c.e.-complete, even inside every open ball;
the precision threshold $1/(qD^n)$ turns approximation into exact synthesis; the
maximal synthesis depth has Turing degree $\mathbf0'$; and the commuting
free-factor mechanism needs dimension four.
\end{itemize}
The two directions of the compiler are Theorem~\ref{pqc:rr:thm:membership}
(membership reduces to one word-problem query) and
Theorem~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:compiler} (the word problem reduces to membership).
Both certificate families are kept (Sections~\ref{pqc:rr:sec:certificates}
and~\ref{pqc:dr:sec:certificates}): source~11 certifies a \emph{state} transfer
with $(k+5)T+5$ integer variables, source~16 a \emph{matrix} synthesis with
$n(s+17)$ natural witnesses and shifted entries in place of signed pairs.

Neither source gives an explicit gate count for its universal instance (both
gate lists depend on an unprinted Higman presentation), so neither bears on the
seven-outcome, dimension-four numbers of Part~II's quantum mortality
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:qm:thm:47}). The predicates also differ: Part~II asks for a
word whose product is \emph{zero}, which is impossible in an orthogonal group;
here the question is membership of a target in the generated group, or
reachability of a target state. Undecidability of rotation reachability on the
three-sphere is not new (Bell and Potapov); both sources say so.

\subsection{The exact--approximate boundary}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-VI:boundary}
Source~10's Theorem~\ref{pqc:cc:thm:cauchy} and source~16's
Theorems~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:net}, \ref{pqc:dr:thm:local} and~\ref{pqc:dr:thm:gap}
sit on opposite sides of one boundary. In source~10 a single rational rotation
is supplied by fast Cauchy names, and exact zero probability is
$\pione$-complete: the difficulty is in the \emph{input representation}. In
source~16 gates and targets are exact rationals; exact synthesis is
$\sigone$-complete, positive-tolerance approximation is computable with a
computable length bound, and the length-dependent threshold $1/(qD^n)$ is exactly
where approximation becomes exact synthesis: the difficulty is in the
\emph{unbounded word search}. Source~11 adds that positive-tolerance transfer is
always possible and that no positive geometric margin separates its hard orbit
from nonreachability (Section~\ref{pqc:rr:sec:bounds}).

\subsection{Letters used differently}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-VI:letters}
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}lYYYY@{}}

$h,H$ & $H$ Hadamard gate; $H_j$ numerators & $h$ number of Hadamards; $H$, $H_R$, $H_*$ height bounds; $H_t(z)$ halting probability by step $t$ & $h_t$ scales; $H$ an exponent & ---\\

$a,b$ & --- & real coordinates of $U_B=a+b\sqrt2$ & letters and quaternions $(3\pm4i)/5$, $(3\pm4j)/5$ & the same\\

The tempting false readings are these. Source~10's $T$ in $8\Lleaf+64\Tmul$ is

\subsection{Abstracts and status statements of the sources}
\paragraph{Abstract of source 10.}
% --- source 10, lines 82-103 ---
A certificate for one legal computational path does not, by itself, certify a
quantum outcome: legal paths may cancel. We construct natural-number
Diophantine certificates for the entire coherent contraction instead. A supplied
binary contraction tree for an integer tensor network gives a quadratic system
with a unique witness, and hence one sum-of-squares polynomial of degree at most
four. An explicit lift to $\Z[e^{i\pi/4}]$ uses at most $8\Lleaf+64\Tmul$ natural variables,
where $\Lleaf$ counts leaf entries and $\Tmul$ counts contraction summands. Every coordinate
has a proved height bound. A canonical quadratic comparison circuit for
$\Q(\sqrt2)$ adds at most 39 variables and 50 equations to certify a strict
rational threshold for an exact quantum probability. We apply the construction
to Clifford+T-type circuits and to adaptive equatorial measurements of graph
states.

Two limitations make the representation meaningful. A uniformly polynomial-size,
polynomial-bit witness compiler for zero output probability would imply
$\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{coNP}$. More fundamentally, with gate parameters supplied by
fast Cauchy names, zero probability is not even computably enumerable on a
uniformly valid family of single-qubit rational rotations. Finally, for
unbounded algebraic quantum controllers, positive-probability halting is
Diophantine by MRDP, whereas almost-sure halting is $\Pi^0_2$-complete.
The article gives full proofs, an executable exact-arithmetic prototype,
reproducible tests, and a formalization and research agenda.
\paragraph{Status statement of source 10.}
% --- source 10, lines 106-111 ---
\noindent\textbf{Status.} The contribution is an explicit compiler and a
representation/resource analysis. Established path-sum, tensor-simulation,
computable-analysis, and termination results are credited separately. Historical
priority for the combined construction has not been established. No new Lean
formalization or resolution of the general finite-fold or single-fold MRDP
conjectures is claimed.
\paragraph{Abstract of source 11.}
% --- source 11, lines 70-95 ---
We construct a fixed finite symmetric family of four-dimensional rotations
with entries in $\Z[1/5]$ for which exact matrix membership is decidable in
polynomial time, but exact transfer from one fixed rational unit vector is
computably enumerable complete. For the same family, transfer from a second
fixed rational vector is polynomial-time decidable. Both orbits are dense,
the generated group is dense in $\SO(4)$, and every positive-tolerance transfer
is possible with a computable uniform bound on control length. The hard
queries can be restricted to a rational target sequence whose four
coordinates satisfy a common constant-coefficient recurrence of order at
most five. In contrast to approximate control, neither the word length nor
the matrix denominator needed for exact transfer admits a recursive bound
in the target's bit length.

The proof gives a uniform compiler from finite group presentations to
rational rotation gates. Its central identity identifies encoded state
orbits with conjugacy classes in the presented group. A modulo-five
quaternion argument supplies an exact decoder, and an explicit inverse
spin calculation handles arbitrary rational matrix queries, including
rotations without rational unit-quaternion lifts. A Miller free-by-free
construction separates the word and conjugacy problems. Finally, every
fixed-length transfer has an explicit quartic integer certificate with
linear size in the length; MRDP gives a fixed unbounded Diophantine
representation. We distinguish these statements from previously known
rotation undecidability and from unresolved finite-fold questions. Exact
Python implementations and finite verification results accompany the
article; the new development has not been checked in Lean.
\paragraph{Status statement of source 11.}
% --- source 11, lines 99-103 ---
\noindent\textbf{Status.} The contribution is a proved structural synthesis
and explicit algorithmic refinement. Historical priority for the full
combination of properties is not asserted. The fixed hard instance uses a
classical finite-presentation existence theorem; its entire numerical gate
list is not expanded in this package.
\paragraph{Abstract of source 16.}
% --- source 16, lines 64-91 ---
We give a presentation-to-rotation compiler that turns the word problem of a
finitely presented group into exact synthesis with finitely many rational
four-dimensional rotations. All gate entries belong to $\Z[1/5]$, all gates
are reversible, and the generated group is dense in $\SO(4)$ whenever the
presentation has a nontrivial relation. A universal specialization has a
computably enumerable complete exact-synthesis problem. After adjoining one
free generator to the source presentation, completeness persists inside
\emph{every prescribed rational open ball} of rotations. In contrast,
arbitrary positive-tolerance approximation is computable, even with a
computable uniform length bound. A length-dependent rational separation
threshold identifies precisely where approximation becomes exact synthesis.

The arithmetic core is an elementary modulo-$5$ proof that a freely reduced
word of length $n$ in $(3+4i)/5$ and $(3+4j)/5$ has least common denominator
exactly $5^n$. The same calculation decodes the word. For a fixed labeled
alphabet of $s$ gates and horizon $n$, we construct a quartic Diophantine
polynomial with $n(s+17)$ natural witnesses whose zeros are in bijection
with the successful labeled gate words. This direct construction is distinct
from the fixed-arity, unbounded representation supplied by MRDP.

The foundational inputs are classical: free-product normal forms, Higman's
embedding theorem, Mihailova's fiber product, and MRDP. The contribution
pursued here is their explicit arithmetic and local-topological combination,
with full proofs of the stated refinements and executable finite checks.
Historical priority for this package has not been established. The universal
specialization is an existence theorem; a concrete small universal
presentation, a fully expanded universal polynomial, and a Lean
formalization are not supplied.
