\section{Conclusions of Part VII}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-VII:conclusions}
% --- source 14, lines 1371-1388 ---
\subsection{Source 14}

The construction separates three tasks that are easy to conflate: locating
a limit, predicting an exact transient observation, and representing a
finite computation arithmetically. The limit is the known point zero and is
approached at an explicit geometric rate. A single half-space observation
can still encode the halting problem. Every bounded observation has a
canonical quartic certificate, while the unbounded existential description
uses MRDP and does not inherit uniqueness for free.

The strongest operational lesson is that global stability is not an exact
verification theorem. Even rationality of every peak value, a computable
Lipschitz bound, and a uniform effective approximation scheme do not supply
a rational-input zero test. The proofs identify where the missing
information lives: in arbitrarily small positive amplitudes and in the
singular projective decoding at the attracting apex.

\clearpage
% --- source 12, lines 1472-1497 ---
\subsection{Source 12}
The main construction separates three ideas that are often bundled
together: local numerical stability, finite-state digit realization, and
exact termination of an unbounded computation. A fixed finite transducer
can induce a global strict contraction on $\Ztwo$ while its iterated
natural-number dynamics has a complete recursively enumerable extinction
set. Every finite quotient is nevertheless nilpotent with an explicit
precision-dependent bound.

The radial clock exposes a second separation. It changes convergence
speed without changing the exact computation, and it is finite-state
exactly when its added delay is eventually periodic. Differentiability at
zero instead requires the added delay to tend to infinity. Arbitrarily strong
asymptotic flatness at the attracting fixed point does not remove the
hardness, whereas scalar analyticity does: an analytic contraction has a
uniform finite extinction horizon, explicitly computable for rational
polynomials under the stated hypotheses.

The Diophantine conclusion is not only an appeal to universality. The
article provides an executable bounded compiler with exact counts,
clock-independent normalized traces, and unique witnesses. Its boundary
with fixed-arity unbounded representation is stated explicitly. The most
concrete next milestone is a Lean-verified universal instantiation of the
finite transducer compiler together with the bounded quartic correctness
and uniqueness theorem.

% --- source 15, lines 1453-1476 ---
\subsection{Source 15}

Exact rational neural computation exposes two different arithmetic resources.
For a fixed network, the nonlinear-looking activation is controlled by a
canonical complementarity relation, and every finite trajectory has a
single quadratic natural-number certificate with unique witnesses. Even
real-input finite reachability stays within rational polyhedral geometry,
so a projective quadratic lift remains exact.

When the parameters are unknown rationals, weight--signal multiplication
changes the geometry. Four clipped layers, bounded tied parameters, and a
single positive output suffice to express all of $\Hten$; the direct
integer lift is quartic. Replacing exact output fitting by wholly strict
target conditions restores rational density and a decision procedure.

Finally, bounded state magnitude is not bounded computational memory.
First acceptance forces distinct rational states, and their denominator
support gives a quantitative precision requirement. In a fixed universal
network, no computable precision ceiling can cover every accepting input.
These statements supply a rigorous, explicit neural front end for the
repository's Diophantine program, while preserving the distinction between
proved constructions, existing foundational theorems, and genuine open
arithmetic questions.


\section{Further research questions of Part VII}
\label{pqc:conv:b62-VII:questions}
\wtag\ Source~14 posed ten questions, source~12 twelve and source~15 twelve; all
are printed. A \wtag\ note after a question names the question of Parts~I--IV,
or of another source, that it duplicates or bears on.

% --- source 14, lines 1278-1370 ---
\subsection{Source 14: strict contractions}\label{pqc:sc:sec:questions}

The following questions are left open by this report. Unless explicitly
linked to an external source, they are proposed project questions rather
than claims about the complete published open-problem landscape.

\begin{question}[Dimension and observation minimality]\label{pqc:sc:q:dimension}
Can the point/half-space separation be realized by a rational continuous
strict contraction in three coordinates, or in two, while keeping a single
fixed linear observation and computable rational encodings? The present
construction spends three coordinates on the cube simulator and one on the
radial clock. A solution must preserve continuity, not silently use a
piecewise discontinuous state selector.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:dimension}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[An explicit small universal instance]\label{pqc:sc:q:instance}
Choose a published universal source program, normalize its exact input and
halt conventions, and compile the complete instruction table. What are the
best resulting values of $m$, $B$, circuit depth, number of gates, and
coefficient heights? Small-register-machine literature provides useful
starting points, but register count and instruction set must be checked
rather than inferred from the word ``universal''~\cite{b62s14-korec}.
\wtag\ Compare source~12's Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:transducer}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Encoding cost]
Can a different continuous cube simulator give a polynomial-time map from
ordinary binary source inputs to rational initial vectors of polynomial bit
length while retaining the four-coordinate global contraction theorem?
The family $2^{-2^e}$ proves computable hardness but is quantitatively very
expensive. An efficient solution would strengthen the complexity meaning of
the substrate considerably.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Smooth compact contractions]\label{pqc:sc:q:smooth}
Can a $C^\infty$ contraction on a compact rational region realize a comparable
exact reachability separation with a natural finite effective description?
The homogeneous route cannot simply be smoothed at zero, by
\cref{pqc:sc:prop:rigid}. A successful construction would need to abandon exact
degree-one homogeneity or change the encoding mechanism.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:realizers} and source~12's Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:regularity}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Structural subclasses]\label{pqc:sc:q:subclasses}
Which additional restrictions force half-space reachability to be
decidable: monotonicity in the coordinatewise order, nonnegative neural
weights, a bounded number of activation patterns along every orbit,
or a genuine Bellman-operator structure? The present hats and zero tests
use signed coefficients. The Bellman results~\cite{b62s14-bellman} concern a
structurally narrower class and a different target specification.
\wtag\ Compare, in spirit, Question~\ref{pqc:q:signed}.
\par\noindent\wtag\ \emph{Batch-78 note (2 October 2026).} Answered negatively
in part, for three of the four restrictions taken together, by Part~II of the
sibling report \code{stochastic-and-thermal-exactness} of this category
(Theorem \code{ste:ec:thm:main} and its Section \code{ste:ec:sec:universality}).
There a fixed finite turn-based stochastic game gives the operator
$\Phi(v)=\frac14\mathbf 1+\frac12 S(v)$, where $S$ takes at each state the
minimum or maximum, by the state's owner, of at most two dyadic stochastic
rows with every entry at least $1/(2N)$, and both owners occur. This $\Phi$ is
coordinatewise monotone, has nonnegative coefficients, is a genuine Bellman
operator and a $1/2$-contraction of $[0,1]^N$ in the supremum norm with the
known fixed point $\frac12\mathbf 1$. Yet, for suitable fixed games and dyadic
initial vectors, the strict-inequality observation ``halt-register value
greater than baseline value'' (an open half-space), scalar equality and exact
attainment of the fixed point are each c.e.-complete. The restriction to a
bounded number of activation patterns is not addressed, and the case with only
MIN or only MAX states stays open there (Section \code{ste:ec:q:oneplayer}).
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Relative-precision semantics]
Suppose admissible observation errors shrink proportionally to the radius.
Which machine encodings remain reliable, and what additional dependence on
the counter magnitudes is needed? The control-state margin is radial, but
large counters are represented by very small ratios. A fault-tolerance
claim must analyze those ratios as well as the final halt readout.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:noise}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Geometry of the zero set]\label{pqc:sc:q:zeroset}
The zero set of $\Peak$ is effectively closed, while the positive locus is
locally rational piecewise affine. What geometric restrictions on a
computably compact subset of $\Cone$ make rational zero membership
decidable? Can one give useful sufficient conditions in terms of a finite
polyhedral decomposition or an effective lower bound on positive peaks?
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:boundary} and source~12's Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:measure}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Certificate optimization]
Can the exact gate count $G=9m+2d_M-3$ and first-hit witness count
$(2G+5)T+1$ be reduced without losing canonical witnesses? In particular,
can state selection share more ReLU gates, and can the two natural variables
per gate be replaced by a smaller globally canonical encoding? Any claimed
improvement should provide both a count and a unique-witness proof at
zero-valued gates.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:smaller} and source~12's Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:smaller}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[A verified end-to-end compiler]
Can ProveIt prove, from one counter-program syntax tree, the conjunction of
exact simulation, the global metric bound, the half-space observation lemma,
and the semantics of the exported quartic? This would turn a collection of
existence arguments into a reusable certified substrate compiler. A useful
first milestone is the three-state transfer example, followed by a fixed
universal source with a separately verified interpreter theorem.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:compiler}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Fixed-arity witness behavior]
Which restricted source-program classes admit fixed-arity unbounded
Diophantine encodings with controlled witness multiplicity? Bounded trace
uniqueness alone is insufficient. A meaningful advance would identify a
new restricted class where the additional MRDP-style witnesses can be
controlled, rather than claiming a general single-fold result from
deterministic semantics.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:frontier} and source~12's Question~\ref{pqc:ad:q:compression}.
\end{question}

% --- source 12, lines 1338-1471 ---
\subsection{Source 12: contracting \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2}-adic dynamics}\label{pqc:ad:sec:questions}

The following questions are proposed research directions, not assertions
that each is a documented open problem in the literature. The first group
has relatively short, checkable targets; the later group asks for genuinely
stronger theory.

\begin{question}[A completely audited universal finite transducer]\label{pqc:ad:q:transducer}
Instantiate the compiler with a small, independently verified binary
universal machine. Export and minimize the reachable transducer, and prove
its equivalence to the machine in Lean. What is the smallest state count
obtainable while retaining the explicit $1/2$-contraction property?
\wtag\ Compare Questions~\ref{pqc:qm:q:compiler} and~\ref{pqc:cb:q:extract}.
\end{question}
The present archive supplies the generic compiler and a nonuniversal
example. A universal instantiation with a traceable source machine and an
end-to-end correctness proof would turn the existence result into a
particularly useful benchmark.

\begin{question}[The state-delay tradeoff]
How far can $K=r+3$ and the exponential bootstrap bound be reduced? Is
there a lower bound relating the maximum negative tape-digit displacement,
header complexity, contraction factor, and minimal transducer state count?
\end{question}
An immediate experiment is to minimize generated tables for families of
machines, then identify which stored prefix bits are redundant. A theorem
should distinguish a smaller implementation from an improved worst-case
bound.

\begin{question}[Automatic coefficient descriptions]
Can one compute a compact van der Put coefficient description for the
constant-drift compiler directly from the source table, and derive the
clock classification through the corresponding automatic-sequence kernel?
\end{question}
Anashin's finiteness criterion provides a natural alternative language
\cite{b62s12-anashin}. The target is an explicit coefficient algorithm or a
quantitative kernel bound, not a second citation for finiteness alone.

\begin{question}[Beyond eventual periodic clocks]
For computable noneventually-periodic delay, what is the least additional
streaming memory needed to realize $F_h$? Can clock growth or descriptive
complexity yield sharp lower bounds for pushdown, counter, or log-space
transducers?
\end{question}
The finite-state case is completely settled by
Theorem~\ref{pqc:ad:thm:clockclass}. The question is the next level of a memory
hierarchy, not whether bounded but aperiodic delay is finite-state.

\begin{question}[Regularity between flatness and analyticity]\label{pqc:ad:q:regularity}
Is there a globally $C^1$, or a suitably defined globally $C^\infty$,
strict contraction of $\Zp$ whose natural-input exact extinction set is
recursively enumerable complete? Which notions of non-Archimedean
smoothness force a finite extinction horizon?
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:realizers}, which Theorem~\ref{pqc:ad:thm:analytic} partly answers in the scalar $2$-adic case.
\end{question}
Our asymptotically flat map does not answer this. A productive first step
is to analyze differentiability on nonzero shells and identify the precise
obstruction caused by digit interleaving.

\begin{question}[Several analytic variables]
For a polynomial or analytic map $f\colon\Zp^d\to\Zp^d$ that is a global
strict contraction fixing zero, must exact extinction of rational inputs
be decidable? Does a uniform horizon exist under a finite-fiber or
isolated-zero-fiber hypothesis?
\end{question}
The scalar argument extends immediately when a sufficiently small
neighborhood has no nonzero point in $f^{-1}(0)$. The hard issue is what
happens without that hypothesis. Positive-dimensional zero fibers prevent
simply repeating the scalar proof.

\begin{question}[Effective analytic presentations]
For which representations of an analytic contraction can the radius $B$
in Theorem~\ref{pqc:ad:thm:analytic} be computed uniformly? Can a verified tail
bound be converted into a practical extinction algorithm with a useful
complexity estimate?
\end{question}
The rational-polynomial case is settled here. Infinite series require
explicit effective control of tails and of a first nonzero coefficient;
an arbitrary coefficient stream need not supply that information.

\begin{question}[Smaller bounded unique-witness certificates]\label{pqc:ad:q:smaller}
Can one reduce the leading coefficient $3m+6$ in the witness count while
preserving uniqueness, degree four, bounded residual coefficients, and
linear sparse size? Can any substantial machine class admit degree-three
single-polynomial certificates with comparably controlled witnesses?
\wtag\ Compare Questions~\ref{pqc:q:smaller} and~\ref{pqc:qm:q:smaller}, and the sharp-degree question of the sibling report \code{canonical-diophantine-certificates}.
\end{question}
A promising concrete direction is binary rather than one-hot control, but
transition selection and preservation of degree two in the residuals must
be handled explicitly. Eliminating variables by substitution can increase
degree or coefficient size.

\begin{question}[Unbounded compression without spurious multiplicity]\label{pqc:ad:q:compression}
What additional hypotheses on a computational substrate permit a
fixed-arity finite-fold representation whose witnesses retain a canonical
trace interpretation? Can the bounded certificates be compressed in any
nontrivial restricted class without introducing uncontrolled witness
multiplicity?
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:qm:q:frontier} and the restricted-class compression questions of the sibling report \code{canonical-diophantine-certificates}.
\end{question}
This is deliberately separated from the proven bounded single-fold result.
No general fixed-arity single-fold MRDP claim follows from the construction.

\begin{question}[Growing-precision observers]
At time $j$, let an observer inspect the residue modulo $2^{k(j)}$ rather
than at a fixed precision. Which growth rates and input-length allowances
recover the simulated configuration, and what exact resource bounds result?
\end{question}
For constant drift, the unit marker itself moves to position $jK+t_0$.
An observer whose precision remains below that position sees only zero.
Above it, recovering the full finite tape additionally requires its
current length. This gives a concrete starting point for a hierarchy of
observation costs.

\begin{question}[Other primes and other digit spaces]
Develop an equally explicit compiler over $\Zp$ for arbitrary primes,
or over formal power-series rings over finite fields. Which parts of the
clock classification depend only on a finite digit alphabet and a
valuation, and which parts require the binary tape encoding?
\end{question}
The radial contraction argument is valuation-theoretic, while the specific
unit map and quartic packing use binary digits. Separating those layers
should make a generalization substantially cleaner than redoing the
entire proof for each prime.

\begin{question}[Measure and density of exact extinction]\label{pqc:ad:q:measure}
For a fixed universal compiler, what can be said about the Haar measure of
its extinction basin in $\Ztwo$, and about natural or logarithmic densities
of its natural-number extinction set? Can prescribed computability
properties be obtained while keeping the constant-drift map finite-state?
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:boundary}.
\end{question}
The set $A$ of halting or invalid units is clopen. Its shell union
$H=\bigcup_{t\ge0}2^t A$ is open, and the full extinction basin is
$\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{j\ge0}F_h^{-j}(H)$. Thus its part away from zero is
open, while zero need not be an interior point. Undecidable membership
alone does not determine the measure or its computability. A proof must analyze this construction rather than
identify it informally with a halting probability.

\subsection{Source 15: precision is memory}
\label{pqc:pm:sec:questions}

The questions below are specific to the constructions of this article.
They are not assertions that every neighboring literature problem remains
open. In particular, established real-training complexity results should
not be relabeled as unanswered rational questions.

\begin{question}[Formal, source-preserving certificate extraction]
Can ProveIt extract the actual sparse polynomial and its witness constructor
from a checked finite-network specification, with machine-checked proofs of
degree, variable count, and inverse decoding? A useful first milestone is
the scalar lemma plus the twenty-variable example, followed by the
$T=0$-safe induction.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:kernel}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Fewer canonical coordinates]
Can the $4nT$ trace witness count be reduced while keeping an explicitly
quadratic, orthant-nonnegative polynomial and unique witnesses at both
thresholds? Eliminating $C=D-X$ syntactically makes $(D-X)H$ potentially
negative away from valid states, so that naive elimination invalidates the
single-sum proof. A reduction needs a different global nonnegativity
argument or a different certificate architecture.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:smaller}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Rational synthesis without ties]
Which tie patterns are actually necessary in \cref{pqc:pm:thm:synthesis}? Can a
comparably explicit $\Hten$ reduction be made with untied edge parameters,
or can selected sparse tie classes be proved decidable? Copies enforced by
extra exact equations must be counted as part of the architecture, not
assumed automatically.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Closed targets with all parameters bounded]
Can the positive-chart condition $v>0$ be eliminated while retaining a
compact rational parameter cube, only closed output conditions, and a
fixed small depth? The unbounded-gain corollary does not answer this:
it replaces positivity with noncompactness. Understanding this trade-off
would sharpen the arithmetic boundary of exact rational synthesis.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Depth, width, and bilinear structure]
Can the four-layer reduction be lowered to three non-input layers without
increasing the parameter domain or strengthening the target language?
What happens when the number of parameter--activation product nodes is
bounded, or their incidence graph is acyclic in a stronger sense than the
feedforward order? A useful classification should track these products,
not just count all neurons.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Effective open-target bounds]
\Cref{pqc:pm:thm:strict} gives a decision procedure but no attractive complexity
bound or denominator estimate. Can one give useful rational witness-height
bounds in terms of depth, coefficient height, and a specified positive
margin? Bounds should distinguish an explicit margin from mere strict
feasibility, which may have arbitrarily small margins across instances.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Canonical projective scales]
Can a rational-trajectory certificate enforce the least common denominator
without introducing an uncontrolled multiplicity of greatest-common-divisor
or Bezout witnesses? The current projective construction is intentionally
nonunique. A canonical scale would be valuable for counting and extraction,
but does not follow from the canonical fixed-input theorem.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Sharpness of the prime-support height estimate]
For a fixed rational network and denominator-prime set $S$, how close can
first-hit runs come to the order
$H^n(\log H)^{|S|-1}$? The proof counts all admissible grid points, not only
states dynamically reachable by one affine-clipping map. Matching
constructions or stronger dynamical restrictions would reveal how much of
the arithmetic state space can actually be used as memory.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Precision growth for a chosen universal network]
For a completely specified universal network and binary input encoding,
compare the maximum accepting-run denominator height on inputs of length
at most $\ell$ with the associated halting-time maximum. The no-ceiling
result proves noncomputability of any total upper bound, but does not give
a precise growth equivalence or eventual domination theorem.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Proof-producing safety rather than counterexamples]
The projective quadratic encodes the \emph{existence} of a finite counterexample.
Can a complementary certificate system give concise independently checkable
proofs that all inputs in a rational polytope are safe through a fixed
horizon? Rational polyhedral separation is available on individual
activation cells; a useful construction must also account for coverage
of all cells without silently replacing a universal statement by an
existential one.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:extract}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Other continuous-looking computational substrates]
Which exact rational systems with piecewise-affine transitions admit the
same canonical scalar-style witnesses? ReLU and fixed-threshold clipping
are natural starting points. Contact dynamics, reset systems, and hybrid
models require care when a physical transition relation is multivalued:
uniqueness of a numerical output need not imply uniqueness of contact or
event witnesses.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:cb:q:transfer}.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Cost of fixed-arity compression]
Starting from this transparent neural front end, what exact coefficient,
operation-count, and witness bounds result from a specified ProveIt
universal-polynomial route? These are concrete engineering-and-proof
questions. They should be answered for the chosen route without claiming
that the finite-horizon uniqueness theorem settles general finite-fold
Diophantine representation.
\wtag\ Compare Question~\ref{pqc:q:direct} and the fixed-arity compression question of the sibling report \code{canonical-diophantine-certificates}.
\end{question}


\part{Continuous time: rational polynomial flows and global mass-action kinetics (source 18)}
\label{pqc:part:tubes}

\section{\wtag\ Conventions of Part VIII}
\label{pqc:tu:conv}

Part~VIII prints one manuscript of batch~64 in full: source~18,
\emph{Rational Tubes, Integer Zeros: Complete Diophantine Certificates for
Polynomial Flows and Chemical Computation} (batch-64 manuscript~05, dated
30 September 2026, pin \code{6d04e1e38}). For a rational polynomial vector
field, a rational initial point and an open rational polyhedral target, it
proves finite reachability equivalent to positive finite-horizon robustness and
to the existence of a canonical integer error-tube certificate
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:equivalence}); compiles each certificate of fixed length
into a counted quartic sum of squares with at most one natural witness
(Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:quartic}); and lifts every such flow to a rational
mass-action system, with $2d+1$ or $d+2$ species, whose prescribed trajectory is
global and whose linear projection keeps every finite open event
(Theorems~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:globalchemical} and~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:compressed}).
Everything in Sections~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:intro}--\ref{pqc:tu:app:notation} is
source~18's text except the passages marked \wtag.

The tempting false readings are these. Part~VIII's $H$ is a count of steps
per unit time, never a target; its target is $U$, and $U_{ij}$ are remainders,
not targets. Its $N$ counts Euler steps and its $D$ is the fineness of the state
lattice: Part~III's mesh $N=D2^n$ is neither. $K$ and $B$ are integers, not the
cube and the rejecting set. ``Robust'' in Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:equivalence}(ii)
means one initial perturbation and one bounded measurable forcing up to a finite
time $T$, not Part~III's per-step adversarial noise, and a certificate
$\Cert_{E_{\mathrm{in}},J}$ is an integer tube, not a graph cut. The rails
$p_j$ and the species $q$ of Sections~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:chemical}
and~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:global} have nothing to do with the numerators and
denominators $p_j/q_j$ of the initial point in Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:instances}.
The quartic $P_{I,N}^{E_{\mathrm{in}},J}$ is a fourth explicit, size-indexed
family beside $F_{N,m}$, $\mathscr Q_{D,K,n}$ and $Q_N$
(Remark~\ref{pqc:conv:rem:fixedpoly}); the fixed polynomials of
Theorem~\ref{pqc:tu:thm:re} and Corollary~\ref{pqc:tu:cor:fixedquartic} come from
MRDP, are not expanded, and carry no witness count.

\subsection{Abstract and status statement of source 18}
\paragraph{Abstract of source 18.}
% --- source 18, lines 87-112 ---
We develop a concrete bridge from continuous-time polynomial dynamics to
Diophantine certification. For a rational polynomial vector field, rational
initial point, and open rational polyhedral target, finite reachability is
proved equivalent to the existence of a canonical integer certificate on a
uniform rational mesh. The certificate records floor-rounded Euler nodes,
ceiling-rounded error radii, strict containment inequalities, and an optional
positive initial-state and forcing tolerance. Both soundness and completeness
are proved, including continuation before possible finite-time blow-up.
For a fixed mesh length $N$, a quadratic-residual compiler gives a single
nonnegative polynomial of degree at most four. If the arithmetic circuit uses
$g$ signed gates, the construction uses
$2g+(6d+3)N+2d+m+3$ natural witnesses and
$2g+(5d+2)N+2d+m+3$ equations, where $m$ is the number of target inequalities.
The witness is unique once the instance and the mesh parameters are fixed.

A second construction embeds an arbitrary $d$-dimensional rational polynomial
flow into positive mass-action kinetics. Reciprocal rail invariants prevent
cancellation-induced auxiliary blow-up, and one additional damping species
makes the lifted trajectory global without losing any finite event of the
original flow. A common-offset variant reduces the global construction from $2d+1$ to $d+2$
species at a cost of three in its degree upper bound. A simple counterexample
explains why a naive dual-rail split lacks the required continuation property. We then connect the complete arithmetic checker to ProveIt's
MRDP interface, carefully separating bounded unrolling, fixed-dimensional
Diophantine representability, and finite-event universality assumptions. Exact
Python checks, explicit quadratic systems, chemical reaction lists, and a
formalization plan accompany the article.

\paragraph{Summary box of source 18's title page.}
% --- source 18, lines 66-75 ---
\textbf{Main construction.} Every finite visit of a rational polynomial flow to an
open rational polyhedron admits a canonical, exactly checked integer error-tube
certificate. Each fixed-length certificate is the natural zero set of an explicit
quartic sum of squares, with quantified witness and equation counts.
\textbf{Chemical normal form.} Every such flow has a rational mass-action
realization on $d+2$ species (or a lower-degree $2d+1$-species form) that preserves
all finite open-target visits under
a positive change of time and has no finite-time blow-up from its prescribed
initialization.

\paragraph{Status statement of source 18.}
% --- source 18, lines 78-83 ---
Research status: complete mathematical proofs and reproducible exact-arithmetic
checks are supplied. The new analytic and compiler theorems have not been
formalized in Lean or independently peer reviewed. Priority for the joint normal
form is not established; classical computability, validated integration, and
chemical universality results are explicitly distinguished from the constructions
proved here.

\wtag\ Source~18's claims ledger is printed in Section~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:intro}.
Its limitations are in Sections~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:mrdp} (local uniqueness is not
a single-fold representation; the degree reduction is standard; the transfer is
conditional), \ref{pqc:tu:sec:global} (global existence only on the invariant
manifold, no uniform clock bound, no infinite-horizon robustness)
and~\ref{pqc:tu:sec:related} (open targets essential; no equality, Zeno or safety

\section{The question and the contribution}\label{pqc:tu:sec:intro}

\subsection{Why continuous computation is a useful next substrate}
A discrete computation has a finite successful history that can be checked by
integer arithmetic. A continuous computation seems different: its successful
history is a real-valued function on an interval, and a numerical approximation
is not itself a proof that the exact trajectory reaches the intended set.
The productive question is not merely whether the resulting acceptance set is
Diophantine. Once recursive enumerability is known, MRDP already answers that.
The sharper question is:
\begin{quote}
Can finite continuous events be represented by an explicit, complete,
low-degree integer certificate whose rounding, error propagation, existence
obligations, and witness multiplicity are all visible?
\end{quote}
We answer this question affirmatively for rational polynomial ordinary
differential equations and open rational polyhedral targets. We also give a
chemical embedding for which a finite event cannot be lost through artificial
blow-up of the encoding variables.

These are mathematical construction problems, not assertions that the
Turing completeness of polynomial ODEs or continuous chemical reaction networks
was previously unknown. Polynomial ODE computation has a substantial theory;
Bournez's account surveys its computability and complexity connections
\cite{b64s18-bournez}. Fages, Le Guludec, Bournez, and Pouly established strong Turing
completeness for continuous chemical reaction networks under their specified
computability semantics \cite{b64s18-fages}. Our construction isolates the additional
finite-certificate and global-lift properties needed for the present arithmetic
interface.
